Now, don't get me wrong. According to my research, the Intel 5820k processor was almost certainly the fastest CPU for ZBrush. I'm still looking for positive confirmaiton that ZBrush can handle 6 cores effeciantly, but it's almost certain that the 5820k would power through ZBrush progress bars about 20% faster than the 4790k. However, the 5820k is both a little bit more expensive, but the motherboard and ram options were significantly more expensive as well.

CPU Total Build Cost Passmark UB Single core UB Multi core Cinebench R11.5 Cinebench R15 multi

6700k $1273 11928 146 756 9.9 888

Then, when you compared the per-dollar (or per $100 dollar) cost, it became very similar.

CPU CPU Build Value per $100 Passmark UB Single core UB Multi core Cinebench R11.5 Cinebench R15 multi
4790k $100 984 10.7 58 0.8 2.5
6700k $100 937 11.5 59 0.8 2.5

Now, the 5820, still ended up with a small per-dollar value advantage over the 4790k, but the 4790k's single-core advantage was so dramatic that they essentially provided even per-dollar performance, with the 4790k having an advantage in single-core processes and the 5820k having an advantage in multi-core processes.

All things being equal, the tie-breaker is that the 4790k is vastly more popular than the 5820k meaning better community support and a higher likelihood that any known bugs with the components will have been discovered and corrected.

It's possible that I'll regret my choice a few years down the road if I ever want to upgrade to 64GB of ram or get a M.2 SSD for my boot drive, but from where I am now, the 4790k seemed like the safest bet for high performance, at a reasonable price, with a high amount of reliability.

Let me tell you a story about how fucked up our system is, and how much more fucked it is now that we've gotten "reforms."

I spend extra money to get the 'nicer' plan from my company to avoid being put into an HSA, which is effectively a health care 'banking acount' bankrolled from your own money (if you get ill once, you're fucked because it will cost way more than you socked away in your account). This 'nicer' plan has a $1500 deductible you have to meet during the year before they'll pay out any major costs. Regular doctor visits etc. only have a copay, lucky me.

Additionally, I'm enrolled in an FSA, also known as a 'flexible spending account,' which allows you to put money in at the start of the year to pay for medical expenses during the year - tax free. The catch is that you can ONLY spend this money on medical expenses, and only $500 rolls over to the next year, if you have an FSA elected that year (if not, you just lose that money). The $500 rollover is part of the recent "reforms," before that you lost everything when the plan year restarted. This seems like a boon to begin with, but in the end they fuck you with their 'generosity' anyway.

In May, I fall and bonk my head late in the evening. The urgent care is closed, so I have to go to the ER. An hour later I'm declared okay with no procedures done after a doc checks me out. A few weeks later I get a bill for ~$1300 in the mail.

Well, that's shitty. Let's put the ludicrous ER costs aside for a moment, and let's put it on the FSA account, that's what it's there for, right?

Then, a month later, in June, I break my toe, at 5:05 PM, vaguely too late to go to the urgent care again. I go to the ER even though I know the bills are going to be crippling.

I find out later all I needed to do was buddy tape the damn toe instead of going to the ER. This is doubly unfortunate, because my health care plan year starts in June.

A month later, I check my FSA account to make sure everything is in good shape. WRONG. Apparently they charged the bills from May to the NEXT plan year's account, then promptly denied the charges for being in the 'wrong plan year.' I call these fucktards up, get a practically unintelligible call center employee, and ask them nicely to apply the leftover money from last year to the charges, then send me a bill for the remainder. That seems reasonable, right?

WRONG. They can't send me a bill. They can't use the money leftover from last year for LAST YEAR'S charges. I have to send them a check to reimburse them, then wait until September for them to roll the remaining money from last year's account to this year's account, which means I can't use any of it for last year's charges.

The icing on the cake is that my deductible for my health insurance reset in June, so now there's AT LEAST another $1300 dollar bill in limbo (probably more) that I haven't gotten yet because my insurance won't pay anything. I have to try and put that onto my FSA account after the previous check goes through to take the old charges off the account.

Basically, I'm in the hole almost $3000 from this nonsense, and the plan 'year' has barely even started.

Lessons learned: 1. Don't get ill the month before your health insurance plans gets reset, and DEFINITELY don't get ill the month after. 2. If you do get ill, unless you're deathly ill, go to an urgent care facility, even if it's farther away and it would be more dangerous to do so. Otherwise, you'll get fucked up the ass by health care costs. 3. Don't use an FSA unless you enjoy documenting and justifying every single health care cost to bean counters from a third party company that's trying to satisfy the IRS. Even if they say a health care cost is 'approved,' you'll still need the receipt if you went to ANYBODY that isn't a big box store that's selling drugs. Heaven help you if you went to a chiropractor, they'll force you to get a 'Letter of Medical Necessity' from your doctor to state why you needed that treatment before they'll approve the charges.

I'm a chronically ill person. I spend upwards of $10,000 a year to treat my usual chronic nerve and muscular health problems, and this extra shit on top is another layer on a shit cake. I don't need the extra stress to deal with this bullshit, but here I am, ill and stuck in bureaucratic hell. Conveniently, I don't quite spend enough on healthcare to be able to get a tax refund, because the recent "reforms" raised the upper limit on how much you need to spend in a year to get the benefit. Not to mention the fact that to even get it I would need to have every single charge I incur during the year carefully documented to avoid getting audited.

In the end, I think I'm dropping the FSA next year. The 20% tax benefit isn't worth the extra years on my life I'm losing by having to justify my every medical expense to the IRS. You almost need to pay an accountant to work the system, but I don't really have the money for that after paying my medical bills.

What kind of fucked up life is it where all of your 'fun' money is by necessity being put into healthcare, and you're slowly being bled dry by bureaucrats? I tell you what, it's only the healthy people who think our system is working 'fine,' and those numbskulls in Washington DC make this system worse with every law they pass.
